::: {.callout-tip}
## Why This Matters
Applied Materials' largest India commitment to date — a 140-acre advanced semiconductor research park combining cleanroom capability, R&D, and a 10x expansion of India-based supply-chain capacity. Reported from two angles a day apart: Karnataka's government framed it as a ₹3,600cr/1,000-job state deal (16 Sept 2026); the company's own 'India Vision 2035' framing the next day put it at $5B over a decade. Same location, same 10-year timeframe, same focus (R&D + equipment manufacturing) — near-certainly one commitment described at state vs. global level, not two additive investments. Both figures are given here since neither source explicitly reconciles them.
:::

## What does this facility supply?

Semiconductor process equipment R&D, engineering design, and manufacturing/testing of chip-making tools; collaborative R&D space for customers and suppliers on one site.

## Project Timeline

- **16 Sep 2026** — Karnataka government announces ₹3,600cr Applied Materials investment in Bengaluru Signature Business Park (R&D, equipment manufacturing, software), ~1,000 jobs
- **17 Sep 2026** — Applied Materials announces 'India Vision 2035' — $5B over a decade, 140-acre research park, 10x supply-chain expansion — at SEMICON India 2026
